title: Handover record
description: The pre-handover checks a worker made before reporting, in machine form, attached to a result as an artifact beside the gate record. The gate record says WHAT was run; this says why that run means anything. NOT an engine record: `validate` knows task, participant, message and artifact, and an artifact payload is opaque bytes to the engine. Every one of the five checks is required: a missing check is not a passed check, and the only way past one is its `notRun` branch with a reason.

schemaVersion.description: The document's schema version. A newer one is not readable by an older reader and says so instead of being guessed at.

tree.description: The branch sha the checks describe: the HEAD commit sha, `git rev-parse HEAD`. Full length only — the reviewer compares it with the worktree HEAD it was handed, and an abbreviation is a record that can never match.

base.description: The base commit the branch was compared against, full length. Without it the verdict-name difference and the environmental-red claim name no second side.

at.description: Exactly what Date#toISOString prints: the date-time format alone allows offsets.

by.description: The bus address that made the checks, in address spelling rather than participant id.

checks.description: The five checks. Each is either performed — and then the fields that prove it are required and bounded to their passing values — or declared `notRun` with a reason. There is no third branch: a check that was performed and failed is not handed over, it is fixed.

verdictNames.description: The difference of verdict-NAME sets between base and branch. Counts are not this check: a suite that goes 244 to 242 to 246 reads as growth while a guarantee is gone, and a removed test never turns red.

mutationProbe.description: The mutation probe made after the commit: break the code, watch a verdict turn red, restore. A probe that turns nothing red is a hole in the tests, not caution, and a probe that turned the WRONG thing red is the same hole with a green look — which is what `expected` is here to tell apart.

treeState.description: `git status --porcelain` at both ends of the probe. A probe that started dirty proves nothing about the commit, and one that ended dirty left the mutation in the tree.

environmentalRed.description: Every red this report calls environmental, flaky or pre-existing, with the evidence that makes the claim checkable. Red here and green on base is the author's own change.

gatesNotRun.description: Every gate command that was NOT run, each with its reason. The gate record carries one entry per command that ran; this is the other half, and it is what keeps a silent gap from reading as a green one.

verdictName.description: A verdict's name as the runner prints it, not a description of it.

reason.description: Why, in the author's own words. Prose, but prose that names a cause rather than repeating the field.

notRun.description: A check honestly declared impossible here, with the reason. It passes: a form that left no way to say this would be a form that rewards invented numbers, which is the defect it exists against.

removed.description: Verdict names present on base and absent on the branch, each with why it went. An empty array is the explicit `none`; a name with no reason is refused, which is the whole of this check.

tree.description: The sha the probe ran on. The probe comes after the commit: on an uncommitted tree the restore would take the fix with the mutation.

mutated.description: Where the mutation was made, as `file:line`. Not a description of it.

mutatedRunExit.description: The exit code of the check run WITH the mutation in place — not the exit code of the probe tool around it, which in this repository leaves 0 on its single passing outcome. At least 1: a run that reddened a verdict cannot have exited 0, and a run that exited 0 saw nothing, which is a hole in the checks rather than a handover.

applied.description: Whether the mutation actually reached the code. Only `true` is a probe: a run whose mutation never applied measured the unmutated tree, and its numbers are about nothing. A probe that failed to apply is declared through `notRun` instead.

baseTotal.description: How many verdicts the same run reports without the mutation. The denominator every other number here is read against.

passed.description: How many verdicts passed under the mutation.

unaccounted.description: `baseTotal − passed − reddened.length`: verdicts the mutated run never reached. Only `0` is a probe. A run that stopped early prints numbers like `0/1` against a base of 26 that read as catastrophe and mean interruption, so the author does this subtraction and states the remainder rather than leaving the reader to infer it. It is checked at `send` against `baseTotal − passed − reddened.length`. A non-zero remainder is not a failing probe to report — it is an interrupted one, declared through `notRun` or run again.

expected.description: The names the mutation was made to redden, written down BEFORE the run. Optional, because records written by an earlier version carry none; present, it is checked at `send` against `reddened` and every name here must appear there. Without it a probe that reddened the wrong thing is indistinguishable from one that worked: a fixture whose refusal came from the path resolver never reached the gate under test, and a verdict that turned red for a foreign reason reads exactly like one that turned red for the right one.

reddened.description: The names of the verdicts that turned red under the mutation. At least one: a probe that reddens nothing found a hole in the tests, and that hole is the finding — not a handover. More names than `expected` is not a fault: a neighbouring verdict that also caught the mutation is a wider net, not a wrong probe.

beforeProbe.description: What `git status --porcelain` printed before the probe. Empty, and nothing else: a probe started on a dirty tree measured something other than the commit.

afterRestore.description: What `git status --porcelain` printed after the restore. Empty, and nothing else: anything left here is the mutation still in the tree the reviewer reads.

claims.description: One entry per red called environmental. An empty array is the explicit `none`.

assertion.description: The assertion text in full, as the runner printed it. A summary of it is not the evidence.

onBase.description: The same verdict run on the base commit. Without it the claim is a word.

command.description: The command as executed on the base commit, including flags.

red.description: Whether the verdict is red on base too. Only `true` is a claim: red on the branch and green on base is the author's own change, and it is fixed rather than declared.

failures.description: The symmetric difference of the failure sets, base against branch. `branchOnly` is what fails only on the branch — those are the author's own, whatever the run is called.

gates.description: One entry per gate command that was not run. An empty array says every gate ran, and the gate record holds them.

command.description: The gate command that was not run, as it would have been executed.
